summary: Moot under master 8b9ad43 (bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton, 1.198x): pooler decode_32 m=32 already runs _bf16_swapab_kernel at 20.0 us row / 20.5 us kernel vs SGLang 22.0, which beats the TMA split-K kernel this hypothesis would install (20.8 us row / 21.0 us kernel in 4e89311eefdc4bc3). Rebased on master, the change would replace a faster wgmma kernel with a slower mma.sync one on the only row it targets.
justification: The mechanism (TMA weight stream, split-K 2, 128 CTAs, ticket reduce) was plausible against the base it names, 658d63b, where pooler m=32 was cuBLAS nvjet 20.2 + splitKreduce 2.0 us (21.6 us row) against a 14.1 us floor; a 1.061x paired gain on that row was measured. But the base is stale. FINDINGS (regenerated on master 8b9ad43) shows layer=pooler load=decode_32 m=32 at 20.0 us with _bf16_swapab_kernel 20.5 us (wgmma m64n32k16, same grid (64,2), split-K 2, BLOCK_K 256, 4 stages). The TMA kernel's own record is 20.8 us row / 21.0 us kernel and, per the hypothesis's Risk section, it compiled to 255 registers on mma.sync, which it calls 'the floor for a Triton mma.sync m=32 pooler'. So the expected 'faster' on pooler decode_32 has no support against the current incumbent; the expected direction is flat-to-slower (~+0.5-1 us). Weakest link: the 'expected' line compares to master 21.6 us, a number master no longer has. The headline effect would be ~0.3% at most even in its favour, well inside the CI, so it cannot be read from a scored run either.
confounders: bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton (landed, master 8b9ad43): it already owns pooler at 17 <= m <= 32 with a faster kernel, so this change, rebased, would compete with it rather than with cuBLAS. A gate placed 'before the cuBLAS fallback' and after the swap-AB route never fires; placed before the swap-AB route it displaces the faster kernel. Either way any measured delta is an interaction with the swap-AB route, not the TMA kernel's own merit.
bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo (landed, 658d63b): the hypothesis's stated base; it deliberately left pooler m=32 on cuBLAS. That premise was removed by the swap-AB promotion.
interference: No companion makes this interpretable worth a scored submit. The only informative comparison is TMA split-K vs swap-AB wgmma on pooler decode_32, which existing records already answer (20.8/21.0 us vs 20.0/20.5 us). An ab-revert of bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton would only reproduce job 4e89311eefdc4bc3's already-measured result on a worse base. The run is also a scored submit with checks spent, so spending it on an expected flat-to-slower, sub-CI change is not justified.
rules_flags: None intrinsic: the TensorDescriptor over the pooler weight built in prepare() is derived from weights, not from per-call inputs, and warmup uses synthetic x with the ticket counter re-zeroed. Correctness risk if implemented anyway: a third ticket buffer and gate ordering in kernel_fn next to the swap-AB route; a scored submit should not carry that for no expected gain.
open_questions: If anyone wants more out of pooler m=32, the next lever is inside _bf16_swapab_kernel (wgmma path, 20.5 us vs 14.1 us floor), e.g. TMA loads of the weight into the swap-AB kernel. That would be a new hypothesis stacked on bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton, not this one.

Is there a measured paired comparison of the swap-AB and TMA split-K kernels on the same job? FINDINGS numbers come from different jobs (1602a4e947e64090 vs 4e89311eefdc4bc3). The gap (~0.5-0.8 us) is consistent but not paired.
